rules.rationale: The runtime crates are product-agnostic, and only the adapter depends on the supported NMP facade.
The current compatibility shell has no profile-refinement or loading-gate feature to assess.
Nostr history and synchronization stay behind the NMP facade; this runtime does not implement an alternate history scanner.
Relay routing belongs to NMP and runtime-facing requests do not accept relay URLs.
Runtime persistence owns only runtime facts while NMP remains the sole owner of Nostr event and write truth.
Bindings and private surfaces impose finite row and frame limits before data reaches a platform shell.
Runtime failures are typed inside Rust and provider refusals are mapped to bounded bridge envelopes rather than an unbounded platform exception channel.
The native host owns WebKit execution and reports bounded raw envelopes; policy and session authority remain outside the napplet frame.
Resource classes, sessions, bridge frames, and work admission have finite limits with observable refusal and event-driven teardown.
Deterministic protocol scenarios use an explicit manual clock; scanner warnings for monotonic synchronization deadlines remain visible in the generated report.
The M0 provider matrix advertises no private-message provider surface, so no runtime privacy fallback is exposed.
